records.exact_relevance: Primary source extending effective measure/randomness machinery beyond Cantor space.
inspected_claims: A computable metric space is a complete separable metric space with a numbered dense ideal set whose pairwise distances are uniformly computable; points use the canonical fast-Cauchy representation.

A probability measure is computable as a computable point of the Prokhorov-metric space of Borel probabilities; equivalently, its valuation on open sets is lower semicomputable, uniformly on finite unions of ideal balls.
On Cantor space, computability of a measure is equivalent to uniform computability of cylinder measures.

Every computable probability space has a binary representation by Cantor space equipped with an appropriate computable measure; the representation has a full-measure constructive domain of unique expansions, with the density qualification tied to support.
Uniform integral tests exist and are universal; fixed-measure tests extend to uniform tests in the source's sense.
Morphisms preserve Martin-Löf random points, and an isomorphism restricts to inverse computable bijections between the random-point sets.

inspected_claims: Theorem 1.1: A⊕B is Martin-Löf random iff A is Martin-Löf random and B is Martin-Löf random relative to A.
Theorem 1.2: A⊕B is Schnorr random iff A is Schnorr random and B is Schnorr random uniformly relative to A.
Definitions 4.1-4.2 define uniform Schnorr tests by total computable maps Φ:2^ω→N^N and uniformly relative Schnorr randomness by the oracle instance.
Definitions 5.1-5.2 define uniform martingale tests and uniformly relative computable randomness.
Theorem 5.3: A⊕B is computably random iff A and B are each computably random uniformly relative to the other.
Corollary 5.4: there exist A,B such that A is computably random uniformly relative to B but not computably random relative to B.
For finite σ,τ the paper uses even/odd interleaving for σ⊕τ: even positions from σ and odd positions from τ.
Section 5.1 states uniformly relative Martin-Löf randomness is equivalent to ordinary relative Martin-Löf randomness.

records.title: The Axiomatization of Randomness
records.priority_relevance: Original statement-inspected source underlying van Lambalgen's relative-randomness/independence theorem, in its actual recursive-sequential-test and product-space formulation.
records.notes: An open University of Amsterdam copy of the 1990 JSL paper was visually statement-inspected. Section 5 defines recursive sequential tests, explains oracle relativization, proves an effective Fubini theorem for product tests, and states Theorem 5.10 in relative-prefix-complexity/randomness notation. P1-S003 does not rewrite the paper as if it stated the later modern A⊕B theorem verbatim.
records.exact_relevance: Original primary provenance for the effective product/relative-randomness phenomenon, while preserving the source's actual notation and theorem form.
inspected_claims: Definition 5.3 defines recursive sequential tests and Martin-Löf randomness via avoidance of all such tests.
The section explicitly relativizes the universal-machine/test setup to an oracle y.
Theorem 5.9 is an effective Fubini statement for a recursive sequential test in 2^ω×2^ω with product measure.

Theorem 5.10 gives the symmetry/independence consequence in the paper's relative prefix-complexity/randomness notation; its proof reduces to x∈R^y and y∈R implying the pair <x,y> lies in the random-pair class R^2.

records.title: О некоторых классах арифметических действительных чисел [On some classes of arithmetical real numbers]
aliases_search_terms: О некоторых классах арифметических действительных чисел
records.priority_relevance: Original 1982 Demuth paper recovered and visually inspected at the pages defining the moving-index/change-bound machinery later normalized as Demuth tests.
records.notes: The source is in Russian and uses Demuth's constructive/arithmetic-real notation. Printed pp. 457-458 were visually inspected. P1-S004 does not claim an independent full translation; the modern all-real Cantor-space normalization in DEF-0026 is cross-checked against SRC-0016 and SRC-0035.
inspected_material: formal definitions around the limit-index and change-bound conditions
records.exact_relevance: Original-source evidence for bounded changes of test indices and 2^-k measure control, with the source's historical restriction to arithmetical reals preserved.
inspected_claims: The original construction uses a limit-computed index for each test level together with a total recursive unary function that bounds the number of changes/mistakes in the approximation.
The inspected definition includes the 2^-k measure control used in the later Demuth-test normalization.
The source's classes are formulated for arithmetical real numbers; P1-S004 does not silently replace that historical domain by all of Cantor space when describing the original.

records.title: Difference Randomness
records.priority_relevance: Primary paper introducing difference randomness, defining the neighborhood-based n-r.e. tests, proving their collapse for n≥2, and locating difference randomness relative to Demuth, weak 2, 2-randomness and Martin-Löf randomness.
records.notes: Proc. AMS metadata was matched to a coauthor-hosted full PDF, visually inspected at Definition 2.3, Proposition 2.10/Figure 1 and Theorem 3.1. The paper also states a modern Demuth-test definition. Its separate 'naive n-r.e.' string-test notion is deliberately not conflated with the neighborhood-based tests defining difference randomness.
records.exact_relevance: Exact difference-test syntax, the n-r.e. terminology collision, strict stronger-randomness placement, and the ML-plus-Turing-incomplete characterization.
inspected_claims: Definition 2.3: an n-r.e. test has components D(W_{g1(i)},...,W_{gn(i)}) of measure at most 2^-i with recursive index functions; for n=2 the resulting notion is called d.r.e. randomness.
Theorem 2.8 identifies all levels n≥2 of this neighborhood-based hierarchy and names the common notion difference randomness.

Proposition 2.10 and Figure 1 state that both weak 2-randomness and Demuth randomness properly imply difference randomness, which properly implies Martin-Löf randomness; Demuth and weak 2-randomness are incomparable.
The paper states that 2-randomness is properly stronger than both Demuth randomness and weak 2-randomness.
Theorem 3.1: the difference-random reals are exactly the Martin-Löf random reals that are not Turing complete.
Earlier in §2 the paper shows that its separate naive n-r.e. string-test notion coincides with 2-randomness for n≥2; this is not the definition of difference randomness.

records.title: Counting the Changes of Random Δ^0_2 Sets
records.priority_relevance: Primary source introducing balanced randomness and fixing its exponential component-change bound.
records.notes: The expanded journal-version text was statement-inspected at Definition 14, Remarks 16-18, Proposition 19 and the later separation discussion. It treats balanced tests as a restricted weak-Demuth form; its pass condition is ordinary test escape, not Demuth's Solovay/finitely-many-components pass condition.
records.exact_relevance: Exact O(2^m) moving-component bound, equivalent exact-2^m normalization, ordinary passing convention, and strict implication to difference randomness.
inspected_claims: Definition 14: a balanced test has c.e. open final components G_m of measure at most 2^-m, with G_m=[W_{f(m)}]^≺ and a computable approximation f(m)=lim_s g(m,s) whose number of changes is O(2^m).
A real passes a balanced test by escaping at least one component; balanced randomness means passing every balanced test.
Remark 18 states that O(2^m) can be replaced by exactly 2^m allowed changes without changing the randomness notion (and likewise by c2^m for fixed positive rational c).
Proposition 19 states that every balanced random real is difference random; later text supplies a difference-random real that is not balanced random.

records.title: Coherent randomness tests and computing the K-trivial sets
records.priority_relevance: Primary paper introducing Oberwolfach randomness via coherent moving-component tests and proving its strict placement between balanced and difference randomness.
records.notes: The EMS full paper was visually statement-inspected at Definitions 2.2-2.3 and Propositions 2.4, 2.5 and 2.15. The definition is recorded in the paper's weak-Demuth moving-component framework, with coherence across adjacent levels; no generalized-measure or oracle version is inferred.
records.exact_relevance: Exact coherent component-change rule, strict balanced/Oberwolfach/difference placement, and interval/left-c.e.-bounded equivalent test normal forms.
inspected_claims: Definition 2.2 places the notion inside weak Demuth tests: each component has measure at most 2^-n and its index has a computable approximation with a computable bound on version changes.
Definition 2.3 adds coherence: over any interval of stages on which level n is unchanged, level n+1 changes at most once.
Proposition 2.4 states that every balanced random set is Oberwolfach random and that the notions do not coincide.
Proposition 2.5 states that every Oberwolfach random set is difference random and that the notions do not coincide.
Proposition 2.15 identifies Oberwolfach, interval-test and left-c.e.-bounded randomness.

records.title: Algorithmic tests and randomness with respect to a class of measures
records.priority_relevance: Primary source for computable-measure Martin-Löf tests, arbitrary-measure uniform tests, and explicit Bernoulli/non-fair-coin test machinery.
records.notes: Statement-inspected from the authors' 2011 preprint/publication version. The source explicitly separates fixed computable measures, arbitrary-measure uniform tests, and Bernoulli class tests; it permits noncomputable Bernoulli parameters in the class-test/uniform framework.
inspected_material: full author-hosted/arXiv definition and theorem statements
pointers: Definitions 2.8-2.11 and Theorem 2.12 (computable Cantor-space measures and Martin-Löf tests)
Definition 5.11 and Theorem 5.12 (P-relative tests and uniformization)
records.exact_relevance: Exact primary support for computable and non-fair-coin measure conventions and uniformity in the measure parameter.
inspected_claims: On Cantor space a measure P is computable when the cylinder-value function x↦P(x) is uniformly computable.
For computable P, Martin-Löf P-tests are uniformly effectively open components with P(U_k)≤2^-k.
A Bernoulli measure B_p is the independent non-symmetric-coin measure with parameter p; the paper does not require p to be computable for its Bernoulli class-test framework.
A uniform test t(omega,P) is jointly lower semicomputable and has integral at most one for every probability measure P.
Every P-test lower semicomputable relative to P can be dominated by a uniform test at P up to the stated constant, and every uniform test restricts to a P-test.

records.title: Lowness for Weakly 1-Generic and Kurtz-Random
records.priority_relevance: Primary statement-level source for the direct comparison weakly 1-generic ⇒ Kurtz-random and its non-converse.

The paper explicitly contrasts dense Σ^0_1 classes with measure-one Σ^0_1 classes and states that every weakly 1-generic is Kurtz-random, while the converse fails.

records.title: Effective Genericity and Differentiability
records.priority_relevance: Primary statement-level source for an exact Cantor-space 1-generic definition and its Π^0_1-boundary characterization.
records.notes: The arXiv/published-version text was visually and textually inspected. Section 2 fixes Cantor-space cylinders, effectively open/closed classes, 'meets', and 'dense along x' before Definition 2.1; Corollary 2.3 gives the boundary formulation.
records.exact_relevance: Pins the object space and dense/open/c.e. conventions for 1-genericity without replacing category by measure.

records.title: An analogy between cardinal characteristics and highness properties of oracles
records.priority_relevance: Primary statement-level source that puts effective meagreness beside effective nullness while explicitly treating them as an analogy whose results may differ.
records.notes: The arXiv/proceedings text was visually and textually inspected. §3.1 defines effective Fσ classes and effectively meager subsets of Cantor space via uniformly Π^0_1 nowhere-dense components; §3.1.1 identifies avoidance of all effectively meager sets with weak 1-genericity. The introduction explicitly warns that meager/null correspondences are analogy rather than identity.
records.exact_relevance: Supplies the effective-category smallness definition and the source-grounded reason category is an alternative smallness framework rather than a probability measure.

records.title: Every 1-Generic Computes a Properly 1-Generic
records.priority_relevance: Later primary source giving exact n-generic/weak-n-generic syntax and explicitly recording Kurtz's interleaving hierarchy.
records.notes: An author-hosted copy matched to Journal of Symbolic Logic metadata was visually and textually inspected. The introduction states the Σ^0_n string-set formulation of n-genericity, defines weak n-genericity as meeting every dense Σ^0_n set of strings, and records the strict interleaving attributed to Kurtz.
records.exact_relevance: Separates 1-/n-genericity from weak n-genericity and prevents importing the repository's weak-n-randomness indexing into the category hierarchy.
